Saturated hydrocarbon: CnH2n+2, all single bonds

Has an −OH group: general formula CnH2n+1OH

walkthroughs.body_html:
Carbon can bond to four other atoms — so it forms huge families of molecules.

Each family shares a general formula and reacts in similar ways. That makes organic chemistry feel like a pattern game.

Alkanes: single bonds only (saturated). Methane CH4, ethane C2H6, propane C3H8, butane C4H10.

Alkenes: at least one C=C double bond (unsaturated). Ethene C2H4, propene C3H6.

Alcohols: contain an −OH group. Methanol CH3OH, ethanol C2H5OH.

Crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons formed from ancient plankton.

Fractional distillation heats the oil — short chains have low boiling points and rise high in the column; long chains drop out low down. Each fraction is a useful fuel or feedstock.

mcqs.q: How do alkenes typically react with bromine?
options: By electrophilic addition — bromine adds across the double bond to form a dibromoalkane.
Bromine substitutes for a hydrogen on the alkene, releasing HBr.
The alkene polymerises with bromine to form a long chain.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.

mcqs.q: When water boils, what is broken?
options: Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen atoms are broken when water boils.
Intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds) between water molecules are broken — the O-H covalent bonds stay intact.
The alkene polymerises with bromine to form a long chain.

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
